detail: England and Wales has no register of judicial interests. Scotland publishes recusals only.
No published register for the judiciary of England and Wales. Parliament publishes one, councils are required to, and the NI Department of Justice does.
Daily rates are published; the number of days each fee-paid judge sits is not, so their earnings cannot be computed.
Arbitration and inquiry work by former judges. Inquiry fees appear in inquiry accounts; arbitration is private.
route: Inquiry annual accounts; Companies House directorships

detail: Published then DELETED: one year for sanctions below removal, five years for removals. The public record of judicial misconduct has a one-year memory. Nobody archives it.
route: Mirror complaints.judicialconduct.gov.uk now; request deleted statements by email

detail: A real one-to-one relationship, but pupillage records are held by the Inns and BSB and are not public.
route: Who's Who; obituaries; interviews; Inn records by request
